requirements.text: The symbol identifying a rear position lamp (steady) (function) for which type approval has been granted shall be R1 (paragraph 5.2.).
The symbol identifying a reversing lamp (function) for which type approval has been granted shall be AR (paragraph 5.8.); the letters A and R may be mingled.
The symbol identifying a stop lamp (steady) (function) for which type approval has been granted shall be S1 (paragraph 5.5.).
Every device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
All markings on the device shall be clearly legible and indelible.
With regard to the size of the approval marking, the value for “a” shall be at least 5 mm.
The approval marking shall consist of the items listed in paragraphs 3.3.2.1. to 3.3.2.5.
The approval marking shall include the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number, being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
The four to six-digit sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the light signalling lamps prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4.
The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
The approval marking shall include the additional symbol(s) of paragraphs 3.3.2.5.1. to 3.3.2.5.3., if applicable.
Lamps which cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately shall bear a horizontal arrow showing in which position the lamp is to be mounted.
The horizontal arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle in the case of front or rear position lamps, front or rear end-outline marker lamps.
The horizontal arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle in the case of reversing lamps in case of reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps.
If applicable, the additional letter "D" shall be shown to the right of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4. on lamps which may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps.
If applicable, the additional letter "Y" shall be shown to the right of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4. on lamps which are used as part of an interdependent lamps system.
Lamps with reduced light distribution, see paragraph 1.1. of Annex 3, shall bear a vertical arrow starting from a horizontal segment and directed downwards.
Lamps shall bear the approval marking.
Lamps shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
Lamps, with the exception of lamps with non-replaceable light sources, shall bear a marking indicating the category or categories of light source(s) prescribed.

Lamps shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage, in the case of lamps with (a) an electronic light source control gear; and/or (b) a variable luminous intensity control; and/or (c) a secondary operating mode; and/or (d) non-replaceable light sources.
In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.

In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the specific identification code of the module, comprising the starting letters “MD” for “MODULE” followed by the approval mark without the circle as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.2.1.1., followed by additional symbols or characters in case several non-identical light source modules are used; the approval mark does not have to be the same as the one on the lamp in which the module is used, but both marks shall be from the same applicant.
In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.3.5. (a), (ii).
In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the lamp shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.

An electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control being part of the lamp, but not included into the lamp body, shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.
The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp which is not designed to be separated from the transparent part of the lamp emitting the light.

In any case the approval marking as well as the category or categories of LED substitute light source(s) prescribed, if any, shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood or boot lid or a door is opened.
If the outer lens of a device is designed to be separated from the main body, the approval marking shall be placed on both the detachable lens and the main body.
In case an outer lens is used for several devices and bearing different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device.
The approval marking and the markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.2., 3.3.3.3., 3.3.3.4., 3.3.3.5. (b) and 3.3.3.6. shall be affixed on the lamp.
The markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.5.(a) shall be affixed on the component.
Where a single approval mark is affixed on grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, it shall be visible after their installation.

Where a single approval mark is affixed on grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, no part of the lamps that transmits light shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark.

The size of the components of a single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
Each lamp submitted for approval shall conform to the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5.

The requirements contained in sections 5 "General specifications" and 6 "Individual specifications" (and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections) of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, and their series of amendments in force at the time of application for the lamp type approval shall apply to this Regulation.

The requirements pertinent to each lamp and to the category/ies of vehicle on which the lamp is intended to be installed shall be applied, where its verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.

The lamps shall be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which they may be subjected in such use, their satisfactory operation remains assured and they retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation.

In the case of a rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp, these functions shall either (a) be provided by multiple light sources (for instance, a double filament light source); or (b) be intended for use in a vehicle equipped with a tell-tale indicating failure for the lamps.

If, on request of the applicant, the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside of the apparent surface of a lamp (function) incorporates a manufacturer logo built by transparent or non-transparent components, it shall be only one logo and all requirements for the specific function of this Regulation shall be fulfilled.

Irrespective of the marking requirements in paragraph 3.3., if a lamp incorporates a manufacturer logo, only the logo of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or the body manufacturer is allowed.

If a lamp incorporates a manufacturer logo, the enclosed light emitting surface of the logo (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) of such a lamp in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 100 cm².
Stop lamps, direction indicator lamps, and reversing lamps shall not incorporate a logo.

In case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source, at least one of the provisions of paragraph 4.6.1.2. shall apply, one being that the light intensity complies with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3 and, when all light sources are illuminated, the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded.

In case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source, at least one of the provisions of paragraph 4.6.1.2. shall apply, one being that a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraphs 6.4.8., 6.7.8., 6.9.8, 6.10.8., 6.11.8., 6.12.8., 6.13.8. and 6.18.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, is produced.

The lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light source(s) approved according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128, provided that no restriction on the use is made at the time of application for type approval, and/or light source module(s) and/or non-replaceable light source(s).
In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the design of the lamp shall be such that the light source(s) can be fixed in no other position but the correct one.
In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the light source(s) holder shall conform to the characteristics given in IEC Publication 60061.
In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the holder data sheet relevant to the category of light source(s) prescribed shall apply.
Light Signalling Devices shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances, which cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that it can only be fitted in the designated and correct position and can only be removed with the use of tool(s).
In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that it is tamperproof.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that, regardless of the use of tool(s), it is not interchangeable with any replaceable UN approved light source and/or any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics that is located in the same lamp housing.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that, when the light source module is removed and replaced by another module provided by the applicant and bearing the same light source module identification code, the photometric requirements of the device shall be met.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, on the reference axis (HV), be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, in no direction where the lamp is visible, exceed the maximum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, outside the reference axis, be not less than the product of the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5., by the percentage specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question, or be not less than the intensity value as specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the tables in Annex 2, be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
The provisions of the relevant paragraphs of Annex 3 on local variations of intensity shall be observed.

If the applicant requests the additional test to verify the visibility of white light towards the rear of a vehicle required in UN Regulation No.48, in the angular field from 165° to 180° outboard in horizontal direction and -2.5° to +5° in vertical direction, the maximum intensity shall be not more than 2.5∙10⁻¹cd; this additional test may be conducted taking into account the influence of the vehicle body.

If a rear position lamp and/or a rear end-outline marker lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp producing either steady or variable luminous intensity, the ratio between the luminous intensities actually measured of the two lamps when turned on simultaneously at the intensity of the rear position lamp or end-outline marker lamp when turned on alone should be at least 5:1 in the field delimited by the straight horizontal lines passing through ±5° V and the straight vertical lines passing through ±10° H of the light distribution table.
Outside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in the relevant paragraph of Annex 3, no sharp variation of colour shall be observed in the light emitted.
The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of the rear position lamp shall meet the requirements in Table 4.

A rear position lamp of category R1, MR or RM1 (steady) shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 4∙10⁰ cd, a maximum luminous intensity of 1.7∙10¹ cd as a single lamp or 8.5∙10⁰ cd as a lamp marked "D", standard light distribution Figure A3-I, and angles of geometric visibility per Table A2-1 with a minimum luminous intensity of 5∙10⁻² cd.
The rear position lamp shall meet the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility given in Table 4.
The rear position lamp shall meet the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
The colour of light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of the stop lamp shall meet the requirements in Table 7.

A stop lamp of category S1 (steady) shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 6.0∙10¹ cd, a maximum luminous intensity of 2.60∙10² cd as a single lamp or 1.30∙10² cd as a lamp marked "D", standard light distribution Figure A3-I, and angles of geometric visibility per Table A2-1 with a minimum luminous intensity of 3∙10⁻¹ cd.
The stop lamp shall meet the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility given in Table 7.
The stop lamp shall meet the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
The colour of light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of the reversing lamp shall meet the requirements in Table 10.

Where the reversing lamp is intended to be installed on a vehicle exclusively in a pair of devices and the photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 30° inwards, a photometric value of at least 2.5∙10¹ cd shall be satisfied.

A reversing lamp of category AR shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 8.0∙10¹ cd, a maximum luminous intensity of 3.00∙10² cd in or above the h-plane, 6.00∙10² cd below the h-plane down to 5°D and 8.00∙10³ cd below 5°D, and standard light distribution Figure A3-V (angles of geometric visibility: N.A.).
The reversing lamp shall meet the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
The colour of light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.

A front/rear position lamp (A, R1, R2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard / 80° outboard (20°/80° with reduced angles used only below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm) and minimum vertical angles of 15° above / 15° below (15°/5° for H-plane mounting height less than 750 mm; 5°/15° for optional lamps with the H-plane at a mounting height of more than 2,100 mm).

A stop lamp (S1, S2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard / 45° outboard (20°/45° with reduced angles used only below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm) and minimum vertical angles of 15° above / 15° below (15°/5° for H-plane mounting height less than 750 mm; 5°/15° for optional lamps with the H-plane at a mounting height of more than 2,100 mm).

Unless specified otherwise, the values shown in Figures A3-I to A3-XV give, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities as a percentage of the minimum intensities required, which shall be mathematically rounded down to three significant digits.

Where a front or rear position lamp or a stop lamp of category S1, S2 or MS (or another lamp listed in (a) to (f)) is intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity shall be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.

Within the field of light distribution schematically shown as a grid, the light pattern shall be substantially uniform, i.e. the light intensity in each direction of a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall meet at least the lowest minimum value being shown on the grid lines surrounding the questioned direction as a percentage.

In the case of reversing lamps, if visual examination of a lamp appears to reveal substantial local variations of intensity, a check shall be made to ensure that no intensity measured between two of the directions of measurement referred to above is below 50 per cent of the lower minimum intensity of the two prescribed for these directions of measurement.

The light distribution of rear position lamps and stop lamps (S1, S2) shall meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I, whose values give, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities as a percentage of the minimum intensities required (see Tables 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8).

The light distribution of reversing lamps shall meet Figure A3-V, whose values (in cd) give, for the various directions of measurement relative to the axis of reference (H = 0° and V = 0°), the minimum intensities of the light emitted.

For reversing lamps and manoeuvring lamps using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and after 10 minutes of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

For all other lamps (functions) using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

Depending on the light source technology, the luminous intensity distribution of the lamp (function) shall, in addition to paragraph 1, be checked for compliance at the point in time listed in Table A8-1.
The luminous intensity distribution of a front and rear position lamp shall be checked for compliance 4 seconds after switch ON at reference coordinate HV.
The luminous intensity distribution of a stop lamp shall be checked for compliance 0.2 seconds after switch ON at reference coordinate HV.
The luminous intensity distribution of a reversing lamp shall be checked for compliance 0.2 seconds after switch ON at reference coordinate HV.

Every retro-reflective device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the Unique Identifier as referred to in the 1958 Agreement and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2. or, the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2.
All markings shall be clearly legible and indelible.
The size of the approval marking shall conform to the value for “a” defined in Table 1.
The approval marking shall consist of the elements listed in paragraphs 3.3.2.1. to 3.3.2.4.
The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
The approval marking shall consist of the four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
The four to six-digit sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
The approval marking shall consist of the symbols identifying the retro-reflective device prescribed in paragraph 3.2.5.
The approval marking shall consist of the number of this Regulation followed by the letter “R” and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
Where the Unique Identifier replaces the approval marking, the Unique Identifier mark shall follow the format in the example shown in Figure I.
Retro-reflective devices shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
Retro-reflective devices shall bear the markings set out in paragraphs 3.3.4.2.1. to 3.3.4.2.3.

In case of a retro-reflector of Class IA, IIIA, IB, IIIB or IVA, the retro-reflective device shall bear the word “TOP” inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.
The approval marking or the Unique Identifier and the markings in paragraphs 3.3.4. shall be clearly legible on the retro-reflective device.
The single approval mark may be located anywhere on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, provided that the conditions of paragraphs 3.3.6.1.1. and 3.3.6.1.2. are met.
The single approval mark on grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps shall be visible after their installation.

No part of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps that transmits light shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or the Unique Identifier.

The size of the components of a single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.

The requirements contained in sections 5. "General specifications" and 6. "Individual specifications" and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, and their series of amendments in force at the time of application for the retro-reflecting device type approval shall apply to this Regulation.

The requirements pertinent to each retro-reflecting device and to the category/ies of vehicle on which the retro-reflecting device is intended to be installed shall be applied, where its verification at the moment of retro-reflecting device type approval is feasible.
Retro-reflective devices shall be so constructed that they function satisfactorily and will continue to do so in normal use.
Retro-reflective devices shall not have any defect in design or manufacture that is detrimental to their efficient operation or to their maintenance in good condition.
The components of retro-reflective devices or parts thereof shall not be capable of being easily dismantled.
The outer surface of retro-reflective devices shall be easy to clean.
The outer surface of retro-reflective devices shall not be rough and any protuberances they may exhibit shall not prevent easy cleaning.
There shall be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflectors when in normal use.
Where a retro-reflector consists of a combined retro-reflecting optical unit and filter, they shall be so designed that they cannot be separated under normal conditions of use.
Retro-reflecting optical units and filters shall not be coloured by means of paint or varnish.

The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous intensity shall be within the limits for the night-time colour of the light retro-reflected from that device, as defined in UN Regulation No. 48.
Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the dimensions and shape requirements set forth in Annex 5.
Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements as specified in paragraphs 5.1.4. to 5.1.5.

Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the physical and mechanical requirements set forth in paragraph 5.1.7., depending on the nature of the materials and construction of the retro-reflective devices.

After verification of the general specifications (paragraph 4.) and the specifications of shape and dimensions (Annex 5), the ten samples shall be subjected to the heat resistance test described in Part 1 of Annex 6.

The two samples of the first group shall be subjected successively to the water penetration test (Part 2 of Annex 6) and then, if this test is satisfactory, to the tests for resistance to fuels and lubricants (Parts 1 and 2 of Annex 7).

The two samples of the second group shall, if necessary, be subjected to the corrosion test in Part 4 of Annex 6, and then to the abrasive-strength test of the rear face of the retro-reflective device in Part 5 of Annex 6.
The two samples of the third group shall be subjected to the test for stability in time of the optical properties of retro-reflective device in Part 3 of Annex 4.
The two samples of the fourth group shall be subjected to the resistance to weathering test (Part 6 of Annex 6).
After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group shall have the colour and RI specified in paragraphs 5.1.3.2.1. and 5.1.3.2.2.
After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group shall have a colour which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.5.
After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group shall have a RI which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.4.

When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values for red retro-reflectors of Class IA and IB shall be equal to or greater than those in Table 3, expressed in millicandelas per lux, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.

RI values of the retro-reflector lower than those shown in the last two columns of Table 3 shall not be permissible within the solid angle having the centre of reference as its apex and bounded by the planes intersecting along the lines (β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°) and (β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°).
For Class IA and IB red retro-reflectors, at angle of divergence α 20', RI shall be at least 3.00∙10² mcd∙lx⁻¹ at β1 = 0°, β2 = 0°; 2.00∙10² at β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°; 1.00∙10² at β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°.
For Class IA and IB red retro-reflectors, at angle of divergence α 1°30', RI shall be at least 5∙10⁰ mcd∙lx⁻¹ at β1 = 0°, β2 = 0°; 2.8∙10⁰ at β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°; 2.5∙10⁰ at β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°.

In the case where a retro-reflector of Class IA or Class IB is intended to be installed with its H plane at a mounting height less than 750 mm above the ground, the RI values shall be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous flux of the retro-reflector shall be within the limits for the night-time colours red, amber or white as specified in UN Regulation No. 48.

The shape of the illuminating surfaces of retro-reflective devices of Class IA or IB shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape, as prescribed for retro-reflectors mentioned in paragraph 2.1., from an observation distance of 10 metres.

In the case of moulded plastics reflectors of retro-reflecting devices of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB, IVA, SMV and advance warning triangle of type 1, the retro-reflective device shall be kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at a temperature of 65 °C ± 2 °C after which the sample shall be allowed to cool for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 ºC.
After the resistance to heat test, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, of its optical component must be visible.

Retro-reflective devices whether part of a lamp or not, or a sample unit of retro-reflective marking, shall be stripped of all removable parts and immersed for 10 minutes in water at a temperature of 50 °C ± 5 °C, the highest point of the upper part of the illuminating surface being 20 mm below the surface of the water.
The immersion test shall be repeated after turning the retro-reflective device through 180°, so that the illuminating surface is at the bottom and the rear face is covered by about 20 mm of water.
The sample units shall then be immediately immersed in the same conditions in water at a temperature of 25 °C ± 5 °C.
No water shall penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit.
If visual inspection clearly reveals the presence of water, the device shall not be considered to have passed the test.

In the case of retro-reflectors, if visual inspection does not reveal the presence of water or in case of doubt, the RI shall be measured by the method described in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation, the retro-reflective device being first lightly shaken to remove excess water from the outside.
A sample device, mounted on a test fixture, with the initial RI measured and recorded, shall be exposed to dust as set out in paragraphs 2.3.5. to 2.3.7.

Retro-reflective devices shall be so designed that they retain the prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite the humidity and corrosive influences to which they are normally exposed.

The resistance of the front surface of the retro-reflective device to tarnishing and of the protection of the rear face to deterioration shall be checked, particularly when an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked.

The retro-reflective device, or the lamp if the device is combined with a light, shall be subjected to the action of a saline mist for a period of 50 hours, comprising two periods of exposure of 24 hours each, separated by an interval of two hours during which the sample is allowed to dry.
Immediately after completion of the corrosion test, the sample shall not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device.

The coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas, when measured after the corrosion test and a recovery period of 48 hours as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6, at an entrance angle of β2 = 5° and an observation angle of α = 20', shall be not less than the value in Table 9 or more than the value in Table 10 respectively.
The samples shall be exposed in accordance with EN ISO 4892-2:2013 using the parameters given in Table A6-1, for the periods given in paragraphs 3.1. and 3.2.
In case of retro-reflective devices, the samples shall be exposed to accelerated artificial weathering for a period of 500 hours.

After the wipe with the test mixture and about five minutes, the surface of the retro-reflective device shall not show any apparent surface changes, except that slight surface cracks will not be objected to.
The approval number shall be placed close to, but in any position in relation to, the circle surrounding the letter "E".
The digits constituting the approval number shall face the same way as the "E".
The group of symbols indicating the class shall be diametrically opposite the approval number.

An international approval mark, consisting of the elements in paragraphs 4.4.1. and 4.4.2., shall be affixed, conspicuously and in a readily accessible place specified on the approval form, to every vehicle conforming to a vehicle type approved under this Regulation.
The international approval mark shall consist of a circle surrounding the letter E followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
The international approval mark shall also consist of the number of this Regulation, followed by the letter R, a dash and the approval number to the right of the circle prescribed in paragraph 4.4.1.

If the vehicle conforms to a vehicle type approved under one or more other Regulations annexed to the Agreement in the country which has granted approval under this Regulation, the symbol prescribed in paragraph 4.4.1. need not be repeated, and the Regulation and approval numbers and the additional symbols of all the Regulations under which approval has been granted in that country shall be placed in vertical columns to the right of the symbol prescribed in paragraph 4.4.1.
The approval mark shall be clearly legible and be indelible.
The approval mark shall be placed close to or on the vehicle data plate affixed by the manufacturer.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which they may be subjected, they retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation and enable the vehicle to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
It shall not be possible for the lamps to be inadvertently maladjusted.

For all light-signalling devices, including those mounted on the side panels, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, with a tolerance of ±3° in each direction.

For all light-signalling devices other than side retro-reflectors and side-marker lamps, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3° in each direction.
Any specific instructions as regards fitting laid down by the manufacturer shall be complied with.
In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall meet the requirements of paragraphs 5.5.1. to 5.5.5.

In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall be fitted to the vehicle symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane (this estimate to be based on the exterior geometrical form of the lamp and not on the edge of its illuminating surface referred to in paragraph 2.10.3.).

In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane; this requirement is not valid with regard to the interior structure of the lamp.
In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.
In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics; this shall not apply to a matched pair of a function and/or an AFS.
In case of lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo, only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo can be fitted on the rear of the vehicle.
In case of lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo, all logos that are not vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer logos are prohibited.

Where lamps are grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with one another, all requirements regarding colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and other requirements, if any, shall be fulfilled.
The photometric and colorimetric requirements of a lamp shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which this lamp is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF.

When a front or rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other function(s) which can be switched ON together with them, the requirements regarding colour of each of these other functions shall be fulfilled when the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the front or rear position lamps are switched ON.

Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.14.11.1., subparagraph (a), the apparent surface of which is composed of two or more distinct parts, shall be installed in such a way that either (a) the total area of the projection of the distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projection of the said apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis; or (b) the minimum distance between the facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis; these requirements shall not apply to a single retro-reflector.
Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1., subparagraph (d) shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface, etc.) of a lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.

Any variation of the photometric characteristics of a lamp in relation to the ambient light, as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, or when the lamp is being used to provide another lighting function, shall be in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.
Red light emitted by a lamp fitted on the rear of the vehicle (as defined in paragraph 2.1.5.) shall not be visible from the front of the vehicle.

To verify paragraph 5.10.1., for the visibility of red light towards the front of a vehicle, with the exception of a red rearmost side-marker lamp, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a red lamp if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (see Annex 4).

The electrical connections shall be such that the front and rear position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps, if they exist, the side-marker lamps, if they exist, and the rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
In the case of an interdependent lamp system, all light sources shall be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
The concealment of lamps shall be prohibited, with the exception of the main-beam headlamps, the dipped-beam headlamps and the front fog lamps, which may be concealed when they are not in use.
The colour of the light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
The colour of the light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
The colour of the light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
The colour of the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be red.
The number of lamps mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of this Regulation.
Where a lamp is installed on movable components, the conditions specified in paragraphs 5.18., 5.19. and 5.20. shall be fulfilled.

Rear position lamps, rear direction-indicators and rear retro-reflectors, triangular as well as non-triangular, shall be installed on movable components only under the conditions of paragraphs 5.18.1. to 5.18.4.

Rear position lamps, rear direction-indicators and rear retro-reflectors installed on movable components shall, at all fixed positions of the movable components, meet all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for those lamps.

Where additional lamps for the functions referred to in paragraph 5.18. are fitted and are switched ON when the movable component is in any fixed open position, these additional lamps shall satisfy all the position, geometric visibility and photometric requirements applicable to the lamps installed on the movable component.
When the movable components are in a position other than a "normal position of use", the devices installed on them shall not cause undue discomfort to road users.

When a lamp is installed on a movable component and the movable component is in the "normal position(s) of use", the lamp shall always return to the position(s) specified by the manufacturer in accordance with this Regulation.

The apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of front and rear position lamps, front and rear direction-indicator lamps and retro-reflectors shall not be hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component, with or without a light-signalling device installed on it, in any fixed position different from the "normal position of use". Fixed position of a movable component means the stable or natural rest position(s) of the movable component specified by the vehicle manufacturer, whether locked or not.
If the requirement that the apparent surface not be hidden more than 50 per cent by a movable component is not practicable, the conditions of paragraphs 5.21.1. or 5.21.2. shall apply.

Where the requirement of paragraph 5.21. is not practicable, additional lamps satisfying all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for the above indicated lamps shall be switched ON when the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of these lamps is more than 50 per cent hidden by the movable component.

Where the requirement of paragraph 5.21. is not practicable, a notice in the vehicle shall inform the user that in certain position(s) of the movable components other road users shall be warned of the presence of the vehicle on the road; for example by means of a warning triangle or other devices according to national requirements for use on the road.

With the exception of retro-reflectors, a lamp shall be capable of being made to operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse; otherwise, even bearing an approval mark, it is deemed not to be present.

Where a temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of a rear position lamp is provided, the replacement function in case of a failure shall be similar in colour, main intensity and position to the function that has ceased to operate.
Where a temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of a rear position lamp is provided, the replacement device shall remain operational in its original safety function.

During a temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of a rear position lamp, a tell-tale on the dashboard (paragraph 2.3.5. of this Regulation) shall indicate occurrence of a temporary replacement and need for repair.

The voltage supplied at the terminals of devices which, according to their type approval documentation, have been tested by the application of a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, or in a secondary operating mode or at a voltage requested by the applicant, shall not exceed the voltage specified for the relevant devices or functions as they have been approved.

In all cases of electric power supply conditions not covered by paragraph 5.27.1., the voltage at the terminals of the device(s) or function(s) shall not exceed 6.75 V (6 Volt-Systems), 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems) or 28 V (24 Volt-Systems) by more than 3 per cent.

There shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of the lamp observed from infinity; however, no account is taken of obstacles, if they were already presented when the lamp was type-approved.

All lamps (devices) shall, where applicable, be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations as specified in the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 6 of this Regulation when installed on a vehicle.
In case of light-signalling lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo, the lamp shall be type approved according to the requirements of the UN Regulation No. 148.
The reversing lamp shall be fitted (mandatory) on motor vehicles and on trailers of categories O2, O3 and O4.
One reversing lamp device shall be fitted (mandatory) on motor vehicles of category M1 and on all other vehicles with a length not exceeding 6,000 mm.

The reversing lamp devices shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 23, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

The reversing lamp shall be positioned in height not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground; for category N2G, N3G, M2G, M3G (off-road) vehicles the maximum height may be increased to 1,400 mm.
The reversing lamp shall be positioned, in length, at the rear of the vehicle.

For reversing lamp devices installed at the rear of the vehicle, the geometric visibility, defined by angles α and β as specified in paragraph 2.10.7., shall be α = 15° upwards and 5° downwards, β = 45° to right and to left if there is only one device, 45° outwards and 30° inwards if there are two.

The electrical connections of the reversing lamp shall be such that the lamp can be switched ON only if the reverse gear is engaged and if the device which controls the starting and stopping of the propulsion system is in such a position that operation of the propulsion system is possible.

The reversing lamp shall not switch ON or remain ON if either the reverse gear is not engaged or the propulsion system control device is not in a position that makes operation of the propulsion system possible.
A tell-tale indicating failure of the reversing lamp shall be provided if required by the component regulation.
Stop lamp devices of S1 or S2 categories shall be fitted (mandatory) on all categories of vehicles.
Two S1 or S2 category stop lamp devices shall be fitted on all categories of vehicles.
The stop lamp devices shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, for S1 or S2 category stop lamp devices, the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

S1 or S2 category stop lamp devices shall be positioned above the ground not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed).
S1 or S2 category stop lamp devices shall be positioned, in length, at the rear of the vehicle.

The horizontal geometric visibility angle of S1 or S2 category stop lamp devices shall be 45° to the left and to the right of the longitudinal axis of the vehicle; however, for the stop lamps of categories S1 and S2 mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

The vertical geometric visibility angle of S1 or S2 category stop lamp devices shall be 15° above and below the horizontal; however, (a) where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°; (b) where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.) the upward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
The stop lamp shall be oriented towards the rear of the vehicle.
All stop lamps shall be switched ON simultaneously when the braking system provides the relevant signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.
A tell-tale indicating failure of the stop lamp shall be provided if required by the component regulation.
Rear position lamp devices of R or R1 or R2 categories shall be fitted (mandatory).
The rear position lamps shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

The point on the apparent surface of the rear position lamp in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle; this condition shall not apply to the optional rear lamps.

The rear position lamp shall be positioned above the ground not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed).
The rear position lamp shall be positioned, in length, at the rear of the vehicle.

The horizontal geometric visibility angle of the rear position lamp shall be 45° inwards and 80° outwards; however, where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

The vertical geometric visibility angle of the rear position lamp shall be 15° above and below the horizontal; however, (a) where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°; (b) where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.) the upward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

The electrical connections of the rear position lamp shall be in accordance with paragraph 5.11.; however, if a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a direction-indicator, the electrical connection of the rear position lamp on the relevant side of the vehicle or the reciprocally incorporated part of it may be such that it is switched OFF during the entire time (both ON and OFF cycle) of operation of the direction-indicator lamp.
A closed-circuit tell-tale for the rear position lamp shall be provided.
The closed-circuit tell-tale shall be combined with that of the front position lamps; this requirement does not apply when daytime running lamps are switched ON.
A tell-tale indicating failure of the rear position lamp shall be provided if required by the component Regulation.
The non-triangular rear retro-reflector shall be present on motor vehicles.

The non-triangular rear retro-reflectors shall be two in number, type-approved according to the requirements concerning Class IA or IB retro-reflectors in the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3, or in the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150.

Any additional retro-reflecting devices and materials (including two retro-reflectors not complying with paragraph 6.14.4.) shall not impair the effectiveness of the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.

In width, the point on the illuminating surface of the rear retro-reflector which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

In height, the rear retro-reflector shall be above the ground not less than 250 mm nor more than 900 mm (not more than 1,200 mm if grouped with any rear lamp(s), 1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm or 1200 mm respectively).
In length, the rear retro-reflector shall be at the rear of the vehicle.
The geometric visibility of the rear retro-reflector shall be, in the horizontal angle, 30° inwards and outwards.

The geometric visibility of the rear retro-reflector shall be, in the vertical angle, 10° above and below horizontal; however, where a retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 10° may be reduced to 5°.

In their respective planes, the zones 1 and 2 explored by the eye of the observer for the visibility of a red lamp to the front and of a white lamp to the rear shall be bounded in height by two horizontal planes 1 m and 2.2 m respectively above the ground.

In their respective planes, the zones 1 and 2 explored by the eye of the observer for the visibility of a red lamp to the front and of a white lamp to the rear shall be bounded in width by two vertical planes which, forming to the front and to the rear respectively an angle of 15° outwards from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane, pass through the point or points of contact of vertical planes parallel to the vehicle's median longitudinal plane delimiting the vehicle's overall width; if there are several points of contact, the foremost shall correspond to the forward plane and the rearmost to the rearward plane.
An approval mark described in paragraph 5.3. shall be affixed to every ESA conforming to a type approved under this Regulation.

An international approval mark shall be affixed, in a conspicuous and easily accessible place specified on the approval communication form, on each vehicle conforming to the type approved under this Regulation, and this mark shall comprise the items of paragraphs 5.3.1. and 5.3.2.
The approval mark shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E", followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval.
The approval mark shall comprise the number of this Regulation, followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number to the right of the circle specified in paragraph 5.3.1.

A vehicle and its electrical/electronic system(s) or ESA(s) shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
ESA(s) shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions, for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband limits shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, and 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 6 to this Regulation.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band the ESA broadband limit shall remain constant at 63 dB microvolts/m.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband limits shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, and 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 7.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band the ESA narrowband limit shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured narrowband value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
The transient conducted emission of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 for the levels given in Table 1.
For ESAs on 12 V systems, the maximum allowed positive pulse amplitude shall be +75 V.
For ESAs on 12 V systems, the maximum allowed negative pulse amplitude shall be -100 V.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) as described in Annex 9.
The test severity in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band shall be as given in Table 2a.
The test severity for the minimum test level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band shall be as given in Table 2b.

For the ESA immunity test below 2 GHz, the frequency range over which the 90 per cent test level applies shall be 20 to 400 MHz for stripline, 20 to 200 MHz for TEM cell, 20 to 400 MHz for BCI, 80 to 2,000 MHz for ALSE and LUF to 2,000 MHz for reverberation chamber.

For the ESA immunity test below 2 GHz, in over 90 per cent of the frequency band, the test level shall be 60 V/m for stripline, 75 V/m for TEM cell, 60 mA for BCI, 30 V/m for ALSE and 21 V/m for reverberation chamber.
For the ESA immunity test above 2 GHz, the frequency range shall be 2,000 to 6,000 MHz for ALSE and reverberation chamber, and not applicable for stripline, TEM cell and BCI.

For the ESA immunity test above 2 GHz, in over 90 per cent of the frequency band, the test level shall be 10 V/m for ALSE and 7 V/m for reverberation chamber, and not applicable for stripline, TEM cell and BCI.

For the ESA immunity test below 2 GHz, the frequency range over which the minimum test level applies shall be 20 to 400 MHz for stripline, 20 to 200 MHz for TEM cell, 20 to 400 MHz for BCI, 80 to 2,000 MHz for ALSE and LUF to 2,000 MHz for reverberation chamber.

For the ESA immunity test below 2 GHz, the minimum test level over the whole frequency band shall be 50 V/m for stripline, 62,5 V/m for TEM cell, 50 mA for BCI, 25 V/m for ALSE and 18 V/m for reverberation chamber.

For the ESA immunity test above 2 GHz, the frequency range of the minimum test level shall be 2,000 to 6,000 MHz for ALSE and reverberation chamber, and not applicable for stripline, TEM cell and BCI.

For the ESA immunity test above 2 GHz, the minimum test level over the whole frequency band shall be 8 V/m for ALSE and 6 V/m for reverberation chamber, and not applicable for stripline, TEM cell and BCI.
The ESA representative of its type shall show no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions" during the tests performed in accordance with Annex 9.

The immunity of the ESA representative of its type to transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 16750-2 for starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.
The starting profile shall be tested according to the functional status classification as defined in ISO 16750-1.
The Functional Performance Status Classification (FPSC) as in ISO 7637-1 shall be applied for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b.

For the starting profile, the ESA shall meet immunity test level II for 12 V and 24 V systems with 10 pulses, with functional status B for ESA related to immunity related functions that shall be operational during engine start phases, C for other ESA related to immunity related functions, and D for ESA not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 1, the ESA shall withstand immunity test level -75 V (12 V system) or -450 V (24 V system), 500 pulses, with FPSC III for ESA related to immunity related functions and III for ESA not related.
For test pulse 2a, the ESA shall withstand immunity test level +37 V (12 V and 24 V systems), 500 pulses, with FPSC I for ESA related to immunity related functions and III for ESA not related.

For test pulse 2b, the ESA shall withstand immunity test level +10 V (12 V system) or +20 V (24 V system), 10 pulses, with FPSC II for ESA related to immunity related functions and III for ESA not related.

For test pulse 3a, the ESA shall withstand immunity test level -112 V (12 V system) or -150 V (24 V system), for a test duration of 1 h, with FPSC I for ESA related to immunity related functions and III for ESA not related.

For test pulse 3b, the ESA shall withstand immunity test level +75 V (12 V system) or +150 V (24 V system), for a test duration of 1 h, with FPSC I for ESA related to immunity related functions and III for ESA not related.

The broadband emission of the ESA in the frequency range 30-75 MHz shall not exceed the limit E (dBµV/m) = 62 - 25.13 log (F/30), with F in MHz, for a 120 kHz bandwidth (paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1.).

The broadband emission of the ESA in the frequency range 75-400 MHz shall not exceed the limit E (dBµV/m) = 52 + 15.13 log (F/75), with F in MHz, for a 120 kHz bandwidth (paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1.).
The narrowband emission of the ESA in the frequency range 30-75 MHz shall not exceed the limit E (dBµV/m) = 52 - 25.13 log (F/30), with F in MHz, for a 120 kHz bandwidth (paragraph 6.6.2.1.).
The narrowband emission of the ESA in the frequency range 75-400 MHz shall not exceed the limit E (dBµV/m) = 42 + 15.13 log (F/75), with F in MHz, for a 120 kHz bandwidth (paragraph 6.6.2.1.).
The ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
If the test is not performed with a REESS, the ESA should be tested at rated current.
The limits shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).

The ESA shall comply with the requirements of the chosen combination of the following test methods, at the manufacturer's discretion, provided that the combination covers the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of this Annex: (a) absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2; (b) TEM cell testing according to ISO 11452-3; (c) bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4; (d) stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5; (e) reverberation chamber test according to ISO 11452-11 (frequency range and general test conditions based on ISO 11452-1).
The ESA under test shall be switched on and shall be stimulated to be in normal operation condition.
Measurements shall be made in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range with frequency steps according to ISO 11452-1.
The ESA shall be immune to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply, as ensured by the test method of Annex 10.
The ESA shall limit conducted transients from the ESA to the vehicle power supply, as ensured by the test method of Annex 10.
